issue.title: Six tests in tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py assert an absolute doctor status while reading the host's live plugin entry points, so they pass or fail on installed-plugin state rather than on the tree
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY the sase-p8 land agent on 2026-08-18 as the "SECONDARY DEFECT THIS EXPOSES" clause of a DISCOVERED ISSUE note on epic sase-p3, and re-verified and routed here by sase-p3.15.land while closing that epic. The primary defect in that note (a dangling editable sase-research-artifacts install) is fixed and is tracked separately on sase-pj; this is the independent hermeticity defect it uncovered, which no fix to the install path can address.

THE DEFECT: tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py isolates the CONFIG the check reads but not the PLUGIN ENTRY POINTS it reads. Its only isolation helper is

```python
def _patch_config(monkeypatch, config):
    monkeypatch.setattr("sase.config.core.load_merged_config", lambda: config)
```

so check_config_repos() still resolves artifact-ref and file-hook providers out of the live interpreter's importlib.metadata entry points. Six tests then assert an ABSOLUTE status ("OK", or a specific problem list) that silently depends on which plugins happen to be installed on the host running pytest.

REPRODUCTION at HEAD 11f78656d, workspace sase_12, with a fully healthy plugin install (sase-research-artifacts 0.2.0 importable, sase doctor -C plugins.required OK):

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py
15 passed

$ SASE_DISABLE_PLUGINS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py
6 failed, 9 passed
```

The six that flip are exactly the six sase-p8.land named: test_repos_reports_ok_when_sidecar_is_unset, test_repos_reports_ok_for_canonical_bucketed_config, test_repos_reports_leftover_name_field, test_repos_reports_scalar_sidecar_value, test_repos_reports_undescribed_enabled_lazy_custom_entry, test_repos_reports_invalid_sidecar_ref_policy. Each fails as `AssertionError: assert 'WARN' == 'OK'` (tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py:298 for the first), because check_config_repos().data["problems"] gains rows like "Failed to load artifact provider entry point sase_artifact_refs:research: ModuleNotFoundError" and "repos.sidecar.custom.research.ref.use references missing artifact ref provider 'research'".

SASE_DISABLE_PLUGINS is used here only as a cheap, deterministic stand-in for the real trigger, which is any host whose installed plugin set differs from the author's: a workspace where a required plugin failed to install, a contributor without the sase-org plugins, a CI leg that installs a different set, or a future plugin whose provider registration changes. Note that the default test fixture's existing SASE_DISABLE_PLUGIN_CONFIG isolation (tests/_conftest_runtime.py, added by sase-p3.15.2) does NOT cover this: it suppresses plugin default_config.yml layers only, and leaves the entry-point registry live on purpose.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: before plugins.required existed, a missing plugin was the common case and these tests were red for the same reason (that is how sase-p8.land found them). Today they are green because the install path was repaired, which means the defect is latent rather than gone -- the suite has simply stopped telling anyone that six of its doctor assertions are a function of the host rather than of the committed tree.

SCOPE: isolate the artifact-provider registry in these tests the way config already is -- patch or fake get_artifact_provider_registry / the entry-point lookup so each test declares the providers it expects, and clear whatever registry cache backs it -- then confirm the file passes identically with and without SASE_DISABLE_PLUGINS=1. While in there, check whether other doctor check tests that call a check function directly with only _patch_config have the same shape; check_config_repos is the one with proven exposure, but the pattern is what should be fixed.

task_type_fields.impact: Latent today and load-bearing tomorrow: any host whose installed plugin set differs from the author machine flips six doctor assertions red regardless of the diff under test, which is how the sase-p8 land agent first hit them. It also means these six tests do not actually verify what they claim -- their OK status is partly supplied by the ambient environment rather than by the config fixture under test.
task_type_fields.location: tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py (_patch_config helper at line 12; check_config_repos in src/sase/doctor/checks_config_repos.py)
task_type_fields.repro: Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py` (15 passed) and then `SASE_DISABLE_PLUGINS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py` (6 failed, 9 passed) on the same unchanged tree at HEAD 11f78656d. The six failures are AssertionError: assert WARN == OK, caused by live artifact-provider entry-point resolution leaking into a check the test believes it has isolated.
